intro.h2: Why a robot brand activation works in Monaco.
p: A robot brand activation in Monaco has to compete with a city that already looks like a campaign. Guests here walk past mirrored cubes, sampling counters and LED walls without slowing down. A humanoid robot breaks that habit. It moves, it looks at people, it answers them, and the first person who films it pulls in the next twenty.

The value is not the machine, it is the behaviour we write around your brand. Before the day we agree what the robot says, where it stands, how it greets a visitor and what the payoff moment looks like. Your logo replaces the wordmark on its chest. The lines are yours, in English or French, or both as the crowd changes.

You get a measurable result rather than a novelty. A full day of activation typically produces hundreds of guest videos, all of them framed on your branding, filmed and posted by the people you were trying to reach. Our operator runs it all, keeps the queue moving and keeps guests at a safe distance without ever making the space feel policed.

ideas.h2: What the robot does on an activation stand.

items.p: The robot walks the front of the space, waves at passers-by and turns a stand people walk past into a stand people join.
It holds a pose, tilts its head and waits. Guests get the shot they wanted, with your logo in frame on its chest.
Your key line, spoken by the robot in English or French, repeated cleanly hundreds of times without a single flat delivery.
It passes a small product, a card or a prize into a guest's hand. The handover is the moment people film and post.
Short choreographed bursts every twenty or thirty minutes, so a crowd builds and the space never looks quiet.
Between blocks it moves down the line, greeting people who are waiting so the queue itself becomes part of the attraction.

intro.h2: The reveal moment, built around a robot.
p: A product launch robot in Monaco solves the oldest problem in the room: the second before the cover comes off. Guests have seen the countdown, the film and the cloth pulled away. What they have not seen is a humanoid walking the product down the centre of the room and placing it in the founder's hands.

We build that moment with you rather than around you. You tell us what the product is, how it must be held and who takes it. We write the approach, the pause, the line and the handover, then rehearse it on your floor before doors open. If the product is heavy, we design the reveal differently, because the robot carries light objects only and we will say so early rather than on the night.

Afterwards the robot keeps working. It moves into the crowd for photographs, repeats the headline message to small groups and gives the press pack a second angle to shoot. Guests film it without being asked, which means the launch keeps appearing in feeds long after your film has finished playing. One booking covers both the stage minute your production needs and the two hours of content your marketing team wants from the room.

ideas.h2: How the robot carries a launch.

The opening sentence of your launch, delivered by the robot in English or French before your speaker takes over.
A gesture on the beat, timed with your show caller, so the screen and the robot land the same moment together.
After the reveal it poses with the product and your spokesperson, giving photographers a frame nobody else has.
Through the reception it works small groups, restating the three points you want quoted, word for word each time.
Your logo on the chest, your colours on the panels, so every clip of the reveal is a clip of your brand.

intro.h2: What a robot changes at a corporate evening.
p: Hire a robot for a corporate event in Monaco and you solve the part every producer worries about: the first thirty minutes. Guests arrive at different times, nobody knows where to stand and the room feels thin. A humanoid greeting people at the door gives the early arrivals something to gather around and something to send to the colleagues still in a taxi.

Through the evening it keeps earning its place. It walks between tables, it poses for the photographs people actually keep, and it can deliver your chief executive's opening words or introduce them by name. Because the script is written with you, the tone stays yours: dry and understated for a partners' dinner, louder for a sales kick-off.

It also handles the awkward jobs well. Announcing a winner, starting a toast, marking a long-service anniversary, closing the night before the band takes over. These are the moments producers usually hand to a compere, and a robot makes them land without anyone having to be funny on demand. Our operator is with the robot throughout, steering it and watching the room, so nothing depends on guests behaving carefully after the second glass.

It poses with teams and tables, so the evening ends with pictures people put in a group chat rather than a folder.
If the night has a message, the robot repeats it in small doses through the room instead of one long speech.
A short final show block before the music, so the night has a punctuation mark instead of drifting to a stop.

The operator stays with the robot all day, manages the crowd around it and keeps the aisle passable for the organisers.

intro.h2: A robot at the Monaco Yacht Show.
p: A Monaco Yacht Show robot has one job: to interrupt a visitor who has already seen forty tenders, twenty interiors and every brochure on the quay. A humanoid that turns, greets and speaks does that in a second, and it does it to exactly the audience a shipyard, a broker or a marine brand is paying to meet.

The setting needs planning and we are direct about it. The robot needs a flat, dry, firm area of roughly three metres by three metres. An aft deck, a beach club or a covered stand on the quay usually works. Passerelles, wet teak, swell and open weather do not, so we look at the space with you first and say plainly where the robot can and cannot stand.

Used well it sells two things at once. It gives your brand the most filmed spot in the row, and it signals that the yard or the brand behind it is comfortable with advanced technology. For owners and charter guests, that second message often matters more than the photographs. The same robot can then host your evening drinks on the deck once the quay empties, which is when the conversations that matter actually happen.

A humanoid robot moving among them turns the quiet stretch into the part they describe afterwards.

It suits the audience. Race week guests are hosted constantly and are difficult to impress with food and champagne alone. A robot that greets them by company name, poses on the terrace with the circuit behind it and delivers your host's message is a genuine talking point, and it photographs beautifully against the harbour.

The practical side is simple but strict. We need about three metres by three metres of flat, dry, firm floor, which most suites and terraces above the circuit have, and we plan the show blocks around the session times so the robot never competes with the cars. Our operator is present the whole time, dressed for the room, and works quietly around your service team. Access windows during race week are narrow, so we agree delivery and get-out with your building long before the Thursday.

intro.h2: Gala entertainment that fits the format.
p: Gala entertainment in Monaco has a shape that rarely changes. Reception, seating, speeches, the cause, the awards, the auction and the band. Guests who attend several of these a season know the shape by heart. A humanoid robot does not need to replace any of that, and it should not try. It simply takes one part of the running order and makes it unfamiliar again.

The award handover is the natural place for it. The robot walks the trophy to the stage, reads the winner's name in English or French and passes it over. The whole room lifts its phones at the same time, which is precisely the reaction a charity committee wants when the evening is also the fundraising film for next year.

Around that moment it works quietly. It greets guests at the champagne reception, poses for the photographer between courses and closes the night before the music starts. Our operator is dressed for the room, stays close to the robot all evening and keeps a working distance from guests, so the spectacle never depends on anyone's judgement after dinner. Nothing runs unattended at any point.

ideas.h2: Where the robot fits a gala evening.

items.p: It carries the trophy to the stage, reads the name and hands it to the winner while the room films.
During champagne it moves between groups, greeting guests and warming a room that is still finding its feet.
A short scripted welcome before your host takes the microphone, in English, French or both.
For a charity gala it can deliver the key figure or the thank you, written with the committee beforehand.
Winners photograph with the robot and the trophy, giving the evening a press image that runs further than a podium shot.
A final short block after dessert, so the evening turns towards the dancefloor on a high note.

faq.q: Can a robot present the awards at a gala in Monaco?
faq.a: Yes. It carries a light trophy to the stage, reads the winner's name and hands it over. We rehearse the handover with your stage manager beforehand, and we check the trophy's weight and shape early so the moment is safe and clean.

faq.q: How much does gala entertainment with a robot cost in Monaco?
faq.a: From €2,000 per day with an operator at the multi-day rate, excluding VAT. A single evening, a bespoke script, travel and staging are quoted separately. Send the date and the venue and you get a plan and a price within 24 hours.

faq.q: Can it read the winners' names correctly?
faq.a: Yes, and we test that in advance. Names are written into the script and rehearsed so the pronunciation is right on the night. The robot speaks English and French, which covers most Monaco guest lists.

faq.q: Will it work on a ballroom stage?
faq.a: On a firm, level, dry stage with a step free route, yes. It needs about three metres by three metres to work in. Stairs onto a rostrum are not part of its routine, so we agree a ramp or a floor level handover with your production team.

faq.q: Is a robot appropriate at a charity dinner?
faq.a: It depends on the tone you want, and we will say so honestly. Written well, it draws attention to the cause and gives the committee a moment worth filming. Written badly, it distracts from it. We build the script with you, not around you.

intro.h2: A robot at a private celebration.
p: A private party robot in Monaco or on the Riviera works for a simple reason. The host's guests have been to every restaurant, every club and every villa on this coast. A humanoid walking out onto the terrace with a cake, a gift or a message is the one arrival they cannot predict.

The brief is usually personal rather than commercial. A birthday where the robot carries the gift, an anniversary where it delivers a message written by the family, an engagement where it appears at exactly the right second. We write the sequence with the host and rehearse it quietly before guests arrive, so the surprise is genuine and the timing is exact.

Discretion runs through the whole booking. We arrive without branding unless you ask for it, our operator dresses for the evening and keeps out of the photographs, and nothing about your event is published by us at any point. The robot needs the same conditions as anywhere else, a flat, dry, firm surface of roughly three metres by three metres and no rain, which on a summer terrace above the coast is rarely a problem. We check the route from the gate to the terrace before anyone arrives.

ideas.h2: What it does at a private party.

items.p: The robot walks the cake or the gift to the guest of honour, which is the clip the whole family keeps.
Words written by you, spoken by the robot in English or French, at the exact moment the room goes quiet.
It welcomes guests as they arrive at the villa or the apartment, so the evening starts with a surprise.
Between courses and after dinner it poses with guests, who leave with something better than another terrace picture.
A short choreographed block when the music starts, which is usually the point the party properly begins.
A ring box, an envelope, a key, a small gift. The handover is planned and rehearsed down to the second.

intro.h2: A conference robot, on stage and in the foyer.
p: Hire a conference robot in Monaco and you get two things a congress usually has to buy separately. On stage it opens the programme, delivers a short scripted welcome and introduces your first speaker, which wakes a room that has just sat down after coffee and expects another set of slides.

In the foyer it does the harder job. Breaks are when delegates check their phones and leave early. A humanoid working the coffee area gives them a reason to stay in the building, and gives your sponsors a stand people actually walk towards. With the AI assistant upgrade it can answer questions about the programme and the rooms, and pass anything else to your staff.

The technology itself is often on topic. At a medical, financial or technology congress the robot is not a gimmick in the corner, it is a live example of what the speakers are describing. NOVA, the same body with the full SDK, can be programmed for a demonstration that belongs inside the session rather than beside it, and our engineers write that behaviour with your programme committee before the congress opens.

With the AI assistant upgrade it listens and replies, then hands over to a human the moment it does not know.
Delegates film themselves with it and post from the venue, which markets next year's edition for you.
